verses: On the other side of the sea, they arrived in the region of the Gerasenes.
As soon as Jesus got out of the boat, He was met by a man with an unclean spirit, who was coming from the tombs.
This man had been living in the tombs and could no longer be restrained, even with chains.
Though he was often bound with chains and shackles, he had broken the chains and shattered the shackles. Now there was no one with the strength to subdue him.
Night and day in the tombs and in the mountains he kept crying out and cutting himself with stones.
When the man saw Jesus from a distance, he ran and fell on his knees before Him.
And he shouted in a loud voice, “What do You want with me, Jesus, Son of the Most High God? I beg You before God not to torture me!”
For Jesus had already declared, “Come out of this man, you unclean spirit!”
“What is your name?” Jesus asked. “My name is Legion,” he replied, “for we are many.”
And he begged Jesus repeatedly not to send them out of that region.
There on the nearby hillside a large herd of pigs was feeding.
So the demons begged Jesus, “Send us to the pigs, so that we may enter them.”
He gave them permission, and the unclean spirits came out and went into the pigs, and the herd of about two thousand rushed down the steep bank into the sea and drowned in the water.
Those tending the pigs ran off and reported this in the town and countryside, and the people went out to see what had happened.
When they came to Jesus, they saw the man who had been possessed by the legion of demons sitting there, clothed and in his right mind; and they were afraid.
Those who had seen it described what had happened to the demon-possessed man and also to the pigs.
And the people began to beg Jesus to leave their region.
As He was getting into the boat, the man who had been possessed by the demons begged to go with Him.
But Jesus would not allow him. “Go home to your own people,” He said, “and tell them how much the Lord has done for you, and what mercy He has shown you.”
So the man went away and began to proclaim throughout the Decapolis how much Jesus had done for him. And everyone was amazed.
title: Go Home and Tell
season_line: Jesus has just calmed the storm, and now the boat lands on the far shore in Gentile country, where a man no one can help is waiting among the tombs.
big_idea: Sharing your faith usually starts at home, simply telling the people who know you best what mercy God has shown you.
frame: Most of us think sharing faith means having the right arguments or the boldest personality. Jesus hands a newly freed man a much simpler job: go to your own people and tell your own story. That is still the call. The people around your table already know your life, so they can see the difference God has made. With Thanksgiving tomorrow, many of us will sit with exactly those people. The whole Bible moves this way, as people who have tasted God's mercy pass it on ({{Psalm 66:16|Psalm 66:16}}). So carry an honest, unhurried posture today. You don't need to preach. Just be ready to name what the Lord has done.

carry.text: But Jesus would not allow him. “Go home to your own people,” He said, “and tell them how much the Lord has done for you, and what mercy He has shown you.”

glance.head: A Man Among Tombs
glance.line: On the far shore Jesus meets a man so tormented that no chain or person can hold him.

glance.head: Legion Meets Its Master
glance.line: The demons recognize Jesus, beg for mercy, and at His word leave the man for a herd of pigs.

glance.head: Afraid of the Change
glance.line: The townspeople find the man calm and clothed, and they are so frightened that they ask Jesus to leave.

glance.head: Sent Home to Tell
glance.line: The freed man wants to follow Jesus, but Jesus sends him home to tell his story, and the whole region is amazed.

understand: Yesterday the disciples watched Jesus silence a storm and asked who He could be. Now, on the other side of the sea, a demon gives the answer out loud: Son of the Most High God. This is Gentile land. There are tombs and pigs, both unclean under the law, and a man with an unclean spirit. Jesus steps straight into the most off-limits place imaginable. Isaiah once described a people who sat among graves and ate pig's flesh, and God said He was holding out His hands to them anyway ({{Isaiah 65:1-4|Isaiah 65:1–4}}).

Legion was the name of a Roman army unit of several thousand soldiers. The name tells us how crushed this man was. Chains couldn't hold him, yet one word from Jesus does. The drowning of the pigs shows how real and how many the spirits were, and how completely they had to obey. Jesus, who calmed the wind, also commands the darkness inside a person.

The town's reaction is sobering. They see the man clothed and in his right mind, and they are afraid. They ask Jesus to go. Sometimes we would rather keep our lives predictable than have Jesus change them, even when the change is good.

Earlier in Mark, Jesus often told healed people to keep quiet ({{Mark 1:43-44|Mark 1:43–44}}). Here He does the opposite. The man is told to go home and tell. Jesus said to tell what the Lord had done, and the man told what Jesus had done. Without realizing it, he names Jesus as Lord. When Jesus later returns to the Decapolis, crowds are ready and waiting ({{Mark 7:31-37|Mark 7:31–37}}). One freed man's story had prepared the ground.

word.gloss: The Greek verb means to show mercy, to have compassion on someone in need and act to help them. Jesus tells the man his story is first a story of mercy, of God moving toward him when he could do nothing for himself.

glow: clothed and in his right mind
Go home to your own people
how much the Lord has done for you

god.short: Ask God to bring one specific mercy to mind that you've never told anyone.
god.full: Sit quietly with verse 19 and ask, Lord, what have You done for me that I've kept to myself? Write down the first specific mercy that comes to mind.
god.why: Jesus sends the man out with a story of mercy, not a speech ({{Mark 5:19|Mark 5:19}}).

together.short: Each say one sentence: one mercy God showed you this year.
together.full: Before you part this morning, each finish this sentence out loud: This year the Lord showed me mercy when... Then just say thank You together.

others.short: Tell one family member, simply and briefly, something God has done for you.
others.full: Today or at tomorrow's Thanksgiving table, share with a parent, sibling, or relative one short, true thing God has done for you. Skip the sermon. Tell the story and let it sit.
others.why: The man went to his own people, and everyone was amazed ({{Mark 5:20|Mark 5:20}}).

tonight: Who in our own family has never heard us say plainly what God has done for us, and what makes that hard to talk about?

more.line: God reaching toward people among tombs and pigs
The Lord breaks chains and frees prisoners
Jesus returns to the Decapolis and finds crowds waiting
